{{nihongo|'''Iwato Shrine'''|石刀神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

It is an {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki-listed shrine}}, and under the former {{ill|Shakaku|ja|社格|ko|사격 (신토)|zh|社格|qid=Q10444029}} system it was a {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=kensha|qid=Q90139226}}.

At the annual "Iwato Festival" held each April, three {{ill|Matsuri float|Q11470974|qid=Q11470974}} are pulled.

As for the Engishiki shrine "Iwato Shrine," there are competing theories: in addition to this shrine in Imaise-cho, candidates include the "Iwato Shrine" in {{ill|Azai|Q11556970|qid=Q11556970|lt=Asai-cho}}, Ichinomiya, and the "Yatsurugi Shrine" in Kuwabara-cho, {{ill|Hashima, Gifu|Q819595|qid=Q819595}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Gifu|af|Gifu-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Gifu|ar|غيفو (محافظة)|arz|جيفو (محافظه)|az|Gifu prefekturası|azb|قیفو اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Gifu|be|Гіфу (прэфектура)|bg|Гифу|bn|গিফু প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Gifu|cdo|Gifu-gâing|ce|Гифу (префектура)|ceb|Gifu-ken|ckb|پارێزگای گیفو|cs|Prefektura Gifu|cy|Gifu (talaith)|da|Gifu-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Gifu|eo|Gubernio Gifu|es|Prefectura de Gifu|et|Gifu prefektuur|eu|Gifu (prefektura)|fa|استان گیفو|fi|Gifun prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Gifu|frr|Gifu (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Gifu|gl|Prefectura de Gifu|hak|Gifu-yen|he|גיפו (מחוז)|hr|Gifu (prefektura)|hu|Gifu prefektúra|hy|Գիֆու (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Gifu|ilo|Prepektura ti Gifu|it|Prefettura di Gifu|ja|岐阜県|jv|Préfèktur Gifu|ka|გიფუს პრეფექტურა|kn|ಗಿಫು (ಪ್ರಾಂತ್ಯ)|ko|기후현|lt|Gifu prefektūra|lv|Gifu prefektūra|mk|Гифу (префектура)|mni|ꯒꯤꯐꯨ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|गिफू प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Gifu|ne|गिफु|nl|Gifu (prefectuur)|no|Gifu (prefektur)|nov|Gifu Prefekture|os|Гифу (префектурæ)|pam|Prepektura ning Gifu|pl|Prefektura Gifu|pnb|ضلع گیفو|pt|Gifu|ro|Prefectura Gifu|ru|Гифу (префектура)|se|Gifu prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Gifu|simple|Gifu Prefecture|sk|Gifu (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Гифу|su|Préféktur Gifu|sv|Gifu prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Gifu|tg|Префектураи Гифу|th|จังหวัดกิฟุ|tl|Prepektura ng Gifu|tr|Gifu (prefektörlük)|tt|Гифу (префектура)|uk|Префектура Ґіфу|ur|گیفو پریفیکچر|vi|Gifu|war|Gifu (prefektura)|wuu|岐阜县|zh|岐阜县|zh_classical|岐阜縣|zh_min_nan|Gihu-koān|zh_yue|岐阜縣|qid=Q131277}}. The Hashima shrine is conjectured to be an old site of this shrine. For the Asai-cho shrine, see {{ill|Iwato Shrine|Q11585184|qid=Q11585184|lt=Iwato Shrine (Ichinomiya, Asai-cho)}}.

=== Overview ===
It is said to have been founded during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}}.

The original site is traditionally said to have been in "Shijo" of Nakajima District, Owari Province. The place name "Sanjo" remains in Ichinomiya today, and the area north of it toward Hashima in Gifu is considered likely. It is said to have later been moved near the current site by {{ill|Tachibana no Kachiko|Q1058216|qid=Q1058216|lt=Empress Danrin}} (consort of {{ill|Emperor Saga|Q316654|qid=Q316654}}). The final move to the current location is said to have been around the {{ill|14th century|Q7034|qid=Q7034}}.

In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was renamed "Sanmyojin Shrine" after combining a branch of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}}. This area had long been a {{ill|Kanbe (social class)|Q11589711|qid=Q11589711}} area of Ise Jingu.

In {{ill|1600|Q6720|qid=Q6720}} ({{ill|Keichō|ca|Keichō|es|Keichō|fa|کیچو (دوره)|fr|Ère Keichō|id|Keichō|it|Keichō|ja|慶長|ko|게이초|ru|Кэйтё|simple|Keichō|sr|Кеичо|sv|Keichō|th|เคโช|tr|Keichō|uk|Кейтьо|zh|慶長|qid=Q1328185}} 5), {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|qid=Q171977}} visited and worshiped while marching west. Because he set up camp at Sanmyojin Shrine, shrine buildings were damaged and part of the structures dismantled. After the {{ill|Battle of Sekigahara|ar|معركة سيكيغاهارا|ast|Batalla de Sekigahara|az|Sekigahara döyüşü (1600)|azb|سکیقاهارا دؤیوشو|ban|Patempuran Sekigahara|bg|Битка при Секигахара|ca|Batalla de Sekigahara|cs|Bitva u Sekigahary|de|Schlacht von Sekigahara|eo|Batalo de Sekigahara|es|Batalla de Sekigahara|et|Sekigahara lahing|eu|Sekigaharako gudua|fa|نبرد سکیگاهارا|fi|Sekigaharan taistelu|fr|Bataille de Sekigahara|gl|Batalla de Sekigahara|gor|Popateya Sekigahara|he|קרב סקיגהארה|hr|Bitka kod Sekigahare|hu|Szekigaharai csata|ia|Batalia de Sekigahara|id|Pertempuran Sekigahara|it|Battaglia di Sekigahara|ja|関ヶ原の戦い|jv|Peperangan Sekigahara|ko|세키가하라 전투|lt|Sekigaharos mūšis|ms|Pertempuran Sekigahara|nl|Slag bij Sekigahara|no|Slaget ved Sekigahara|pl|Bitwa pod Sekigaharą|pt|Batalha de Sekigahara|ro|Bătălia de la Sekigahara|ru|Битва при Сэкигахаре|sh|Bitka kod Sekigahare|sk|Bitka pri Sekigahare|sr|Битка код Секигахаре|sv|Slaget vid Sekigahara|th|ยุทธการที่เซกิงาฮาระ|tr|Sekigahara Muharebesi|uk|Битва при Секіґахарі|vi|Trận Sekigahara|wuu|关原大战|zh|關原之戰|zh_yue|關原之戰|qid=Q234188}}, it was rebuilt in {{ill|1608|Q6758|qid=Q6758}} (Keicho 13). === Address ===
* 2 Umayose-Iwato, Imaise-cho, Ichinomiya, Aichi Prefecture

=== Transportation ===
* About 15 minutes on foot from {{ill|Iwato Station|Q11585186|qid=Q11585186}} on the Meitetsu {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Q1137838|qid=Q1137838}}.
* {{ill|I-Bus|Q11223722|qid=Q11223722}}: get off at "Umayose" bus stop on the Ichinomiya course; about 12 minutes on foot.

=== Iwato Festival ===
A festival of Iwato Shrine in which {{ill|Matsuri float|Q11470974|qid=Q11470974}} are pulled on the Sunday immediately after {{ill|April 19|Q2523|qid=Q2523}} each year.

Before WWII there were five floats, but two were lost in {{ill|Airstrike|Q2380335|qid=Q2380335}} during the {{ill|Pacific War|Q184425|qid=Q184425}}, leaving three today.

Iwato Shrine (Asai-cho, Ichinomiya) is a shrine in Asai-cho, Ichinomiya, Aichi Prefecture. There is a theory that it is the Shikinaisha "Iwato Shrine" of Nakajima District, Owari Province. However, this area was {{ill|Haguri District|Q1032507|qid=Q1032507}} of Owari Province, so this theory is questioned. On the other hand, as {{ill|Ozeki Shrine|ja|小塞神社|qid=Q11459557}} in Asai-cho is also estimated to be an Engishiki shrine of Nakajima District, and because this area was frequently flooded by the {{ill|Kiso River|Q779607|qid=Q779607}} and district boundaries in the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} were unclear, {{独自研究範囲|it is possible this area was also in Nakajima District.|date=2021年5月}}.

Every year on the first Saturday of August, the Kuroiwa Iwato Gion Festival is held and one festival float is pulled.

On March 22, {{ill|2016|Q25245|qid=Q25245}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} 28), it was designated an Ichinomiya City intangible folk cultural property.

=== Overview ===
It is said to have been founded during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}}.

The enshrined deity is said to be Yasokikurihime-no-kami, but even now there is no formal shrine building, and a giant rock is worshiped as the sacred body. The sacred giant rock is a glossy black boulder about 6 shaku long and 4 shaku wide, said to shine golden in sunlight; it is also called a胴体 rock. Outside the precinct is another giant rock (tail rock) of about 6 shaku square. Because rocks are the objects of worship, it may preserve an ancient worship form.

In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it is said to have been called "Kuroiwa Tenno." It is said to have been renamed Iwato Shrine in the Meiji era.

=== Transportation ===
* Get off at "Kawada Kuroiwa" bus stop on {{ill|Meitetsu Bus|Q6810397|qid=Q6810397}}.
** From {{ill|Meitetsu Ichinomiya Station|Q2856589|qid=Q2856589}} / {{ill|Owari-Ichinomiya Station|Q871495|qid=Q871495}}, take bus bound for "Miyada-hongo" or "Kawashima".
** From {{ill|Kōnan Station (Aichi)|Q201473|qid=Q201473}}, take bus bound for "Kawashima".

*Note: there are two "Kawada Kuroiwa" bus stops. The nearest to the shrine is on the Meitetsu Ichinomiya - Miyada-hongo / Konan - Kawashima route (about 5 minutes on foot). From the Meitetsu Ichinomiya - Kawashima route stop, it is about 8 minutes on foot.*
